summary: Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Otani University from circa 1925 to 1928. He later held posts at Otani University (~1949–1969) and Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1970–1979).

Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1941 to 1947. He later served as professor emeritus at Waseda University, attested between 1988 and 2000.

Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University (~1974–1985), where he served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism (~2003–2024), and was attested as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai in 2007.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied in the doctoral program at Toyo University (attested 2015). In 2015, he held research positions at Toyo University and the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Hatani (1883–1974) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Kyoto University from 1929 to 1943 and later served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University from circa 1954 to 1974.

Ryoun Yamada (born 1940) studied under Kōun Yamada (~1969–1989) and at Harvard Business School (~1971–1973). In the field of Buddhist studies, he became leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004, alongside a corporate career at Mitsubishi and other firms.

Ryudo Fujii, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Tanemura (born 1970) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His appointments include positions at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuhiko Taga (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his career at Rissho University as lecturer, associate professor, professor (~1980–2001), and university president (~1992–1995).

Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia, learning under teachers including Hakeda and Yampolsky. A scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies, he held professorships at Columbia (1998–2004) and Harvard University (~2003).
Ryukai Mano (born 1929) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who succeeded Yuishin Ito. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1991.
Ryuken Sato (1931–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. Attested in 2014, he served as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans, completing a thesis by 2003.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1955). He worked at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1972–1997).

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Tohoku. He held professorships at Tokyo and Kyushu, served as president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964), and joined Japan Academy.

Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kikutani held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947), an Indologist, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He served as an assistant at Marburg (~1980–1983) and later as professor and professor emeritus (1995–2012) at Tokyo.

Ryō Nishimura (1972–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1991 to 1995 and studied under Fumihiko Sueki between circa 1999 and 2004.

Ryōjin Soga (1875–1971) studied at Otani, Shinshu, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Toyo and served extensively at Otani University, including as professor, professor emeritus (1951), and 17th president (1961–1967).

Ryōshō Tanaka (1933–2016) studied at Komazawa University and researched Buddhist studies and sinology. He became a professor, dean, museum director, and president (2009) at Komazawa, and held posts at Ryukoku University and the Soto Zen Research Center.
